Ancestral contributions define how inherited traits aggregate across generations through additive coefficients. Statistical blending models the mixing of parental traits into offspring, assuming linearity or known stochastic behavior. Deviation schemes describe variability around central tendencies, forming the basis for frequency distributions. These operators form a dual framework: one for deterministic inheritance pathways and another for probabilistic trait expression. Failure modes arise when assumptions of additivity, normality, or independence break down—such as in epistasis or environmental interaction. The interplay between these constructs enables both predictive modeling (GSI) and dynamic simulation (GSE) of trait evolution.
